newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Fahey says Australia economic outlook sound.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Fahey says Australia economic outlook sound.

text.p: Australian acting treasurer John Fahey said on Monday the economic outlook for Australia is sound.
"The outlook for the Australian eocnomy is sound," Fahey told an economist's conference.
He said present indications suggested that underlying inflation was set to fall within the Reserve Bank of Australia's two to three percent objective in the second half of 1996.
Fahey, Australia's finance minister, said wage pressures, although still present, had eased back from the high rates of last year.
"These developments augur well for sustaining solid economic and employment growth over the next few years," he said.
Fahey also said visible improvement in the current account should be a medium term focus.
He said the government's fiscal strategy should help to contain the current account deficit by raising national savings.
"Since the excess of what we invest and what we save is, by definition, the current account deficit, a tighter fiscal policy can be of some assistance," Fahey said.
Fahey repeated that the government's fiscal strategy provided an important pre-condition for interest rate cuts.
